intro.TrustedMarkup:
A parser written from a .syntax grammar, as ordinary Vyrn code.

syntax(path) is a generator import. It writes one parse<Start> for each rule no other rule reads, one type per rule a reader can read, and a Row enum of the rows the grammar names. The parser runs at generation and at run time alike, and no interpreter of a grammar ships.

import { syntax, SyntaxError } from "std/syntax"
import { parseFile, File, Row } from syntax("./json.syntax")

fn valid(text: String) -> Bool {
    return match parseFile(text) {
        Ok(file) => true,
        Err(errors) => false,
    }
}

A grammar states shape only, so the parser holds no sentence. A row is a name and its holes, and the reader says what each row means. A label is a field of the tree, and every record holds its byte span. One refusal of a grammar whose rows are R: its row, a 1-based line and column, and the byte offset past the refused token. A parser answers with its own Row, so a refusal of one grammar is no refusal of another.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type SyntaxError<R> = { row: R, line: Int64, col: Int64, end: Int64 }

The parser the grammar at path writes. A grammar that does not load is a report at its line and column, and the path must be one the generator's caller passed.
